hazards.consequence: A reviewer approves on evidence that was never checked, believing the numbers vouch for the story.
hazards.control: A verified finding is rebuilt from the checked evidence; the proposal's own wording is discarded.
hazards.hazard: A proposal pairs correct figures with a fabricated account of events.
hazards.residual: Only a computed volume variance is admissible. Any other finding type is dropped rather than verified — the runner cannot check it, so it does not carry it.

hazards.consequence: An invoice is accepted on the supplier's own say-so.
hazards.control: Free text never reaches the proposal adapter or the decision; the proposer is handed a revalidated submission with the note removed.
hazards.hazard: Supplier free text instructs the system to approve without review.
hazards.residual: The instruction-pattern detector is two signatures and is not a comprehensive injection detector. Structural exclusion is what holds, not detection.

hazards.cap_reason: The allowlist is a set held by this process. The mechanism — an explicit authorisation check that mutates nothing on failure — transfers to a deployment; the identity behind it does not, and a session or delegation model would have to supply it.
hazards.consequence: A submission is disposed of by someone with no authority to do it, and the record says otherwise.
hazards.control: An explicit Awaiting_reviewer state plus a reviewer allowlist; an unauthorised resume raises and mutates nothing.
hazards.hazard: An unauthorised actor records a decision.
hazards.residual: A reference authorization check against a configured set, not a production identity system, session model or delegation chain.

hazards.consequence: An invoice that failed arithmetic or contract checks is approved anyway.
hazards.control: resume() refuses an approval while failures remain; the case must be corrected or rejected.
hazards.hazard: A hard check failure is waived at the gate.
hazards.residual: Covers this runner's fourteen checks. A check that is not implemented cannot fail, and so cannot block.

hazards.cap_reason: The register lives in memory for the length of one run. Across two processes — or one restart — it sees nothing, so in a deployment this control is effectively absent until a durable shared register replaces it. This is the widest gap in the log and the first thing an integration has to close.
hazards.control: The supplier-and-invoice identity is checked against an approved-invoice register before approval is possible.
hazards.hazard: The same invoice is submitted and accepted twice.
hazards.residual: The register is an in-memory fixture. A deployment needs a durable, shared one, or the check only sees one process.

hazards.cap_reason: Version enforcement and event retention are ordinary logic and transfer as they are. What does not transfer is durability: records are held for the run, so retention and tamper evidence remain integration responsibilities.
hazards.consequence: The record no longer shows what was originally claimed, so the decision cannot be reconstructed.
hazards.control: A correction must keep the case and invoice identity and increase its version; earlier events stay in the record and every check runs again.
hazards.hazard: A correction quietly replaces the submission it corrects.
hazards.residual: Records are held in memory for the run. Durable custody, retention and tamper evidence are integration responsibilities.

hazards.consequence: The case is stranded mid-run with no findings and no reviewer, or unchecked proposals reach the package.
hazards.control: An adapter that raises or exceeds its budget forfeits every proposal, and the case still reaches the gate.
hazards.hazard: The proposal adapter fails or floods the verifier.
hazards.residual: Bounds the blast radius of a bad proposer; it does not make the proposer trustworthy.

hazards.consequence: The page asserts a level of verification that no longer corresponds to anything.
hazards.control: The test count is recorded against a digest of the supplier sources and is withdrawn from the page when the digest stops matching.
hazards.hazard: A displayed assurance figure outlives the code it measured.
hazards.residual: Covers the supplier sources only. It detects a stale figure; it does not detect a test that passes for the wrong reason. It also fires only while the page is being built: a figure already published stays on the live site until the next deploy, so the digest bounds what a build may claim rather than what a deployed page still shows. Observed — adding five tests left the site displaying 71 against a suite of 78 until this deploy.

note: Authored for this runner. Each row carries its control, the test that exercises it, what it still leaves uncovered, and a grading.

scale.basis: Adapted from the severity/exposure/controllability determination used in functional safety. It is an adaptation for this workflow, not a classification under any standard.

control_class.detective: The hazard can arise and is caught by a check.
control_class.procedural: The hazard is addressed by an instruction to a person.
control_class.structural: The hazard cannot arise: the path that would carry it does not exist.

controllability.1: Readily detectable from what the review package already shows.
controllability.2: Detectable only by going back to the source documents.
controllability.3: No signal reaches the reviewer; nothing in the package would look wrong.

exposure.1: Requires an adversary; does not arise on its own.
exposure.2: Plausible in ordinary operation — supplier error, adapter fault, resubmission.

severity.1: Recoverable record defect; no payment is made on it.
severity.2: An incorrect payment, recoverable through ordinary dispute.
severity.3: An incorrect payment AND a record that misstates what was checked or who decided.
